higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall provide the capability to automatically load a configuration of DPU-RTOS from EEPROM to DRAM and start its execution.
lower_level_requirement: Startup Sequence On flight, a power cycle can only be effected by the SCU. A watchdog reset could be induced by the DPU FSW due to a detected, unrecoverable error, or it could occur as a by-product of the FSW entering a state in which it fails to strobe the watchdog timer. On boot, the bootstrap tests and clears DRAM, and then proceeds to load the DPU FSW from EEPROM and executes it. The DPU FSW then loads configuration information from EEPROM (which establishes various operational defaults) and spawns the various DPU FSW tasks.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly describes the boot behavior in which the system loads software from EEPROM into cleared DRAM and begins execution after startup. It further states that the DPU FSW loads configuration information from EEPROM, which corresponds to establishing the DPU-RTOS/FSW operational configuration required by the higher-level requirement. Thus, it operationalizes the automatic EEPROM-to-DRAM loading and execution startup capability specified for DPU-BOOT.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall attempt to complete its normal execution sequence following detection of any failure.
lower_level_requirement: DRAM BITPart of the memory is tested in Boot Sequence 1, and part of the memory is tested during Boot Sequence 2. During Boot Sequence 1, ? KB of DRAM is tested before the Bootstrap is copied to this area. During Boot Sequence 2, the remaining memory is tested in ? KB blocks. The DRAM BIT first writes the address of each word in a block to that word in the block. Then the test flushes the cache and reads back the entire block. If a single-bit error occurs on the read-back, the location is read again. If another single-bit error occurs, the test assumes a hard error and marks the whole block bad. If a multiple-bit error occurs, the whole block is marked bad. If the value read back does not match the address, the whole block is marked bad. This same process is repeated with the ones complement of the address. The Bootstrap stores the results of the DRAM BIT in EEPROM as a series of x consecutive y-bit words. Each bit in a result word represents the result of testing a ? KB block of DRAM. These bits are mapped to DRAM by proceeding from least-significant bit (LSb) to most-significant bit (MSb) as the addresses of the memory blocks increase. A set bit indicates that a block of DRAM has failed. A clear bit indicates that a block of DRAM has passed the test.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement defines how DRAM failures are detected, classified, recorded, and isolated during the boot sequences by marking failed memory blocks bad while identifying passed blocks. This supports the higher-level requirement because completing normal execution after a detected failure requires the boot process to handle failures rather than simply stop; the DRAM BIT provides the mechanism for detecting failed DRAM blocks and preserving results so execution can proceed using known-good memory.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall attempt to complete its normal execution sequence following detection of any failure.
lower_level_requirement: Error Detection and Correction CSCThe Error Detection and Correction (EDAC) CSC is a Level 1 reuse component from the SSFF and INSTRUMENT Y projects. The EDAC CSC consists of a set of Interrupt Service Routines (ISRs) and a Memory Scrubber Task. The design of the INSTRUMENT Y EDAC CSC is described in document CIDPSDS-01.The only design change was to add logic to check for excessive external (SCM) EDAC interrupts.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement describes EDAC functionality that detects and handles memory-related error conditions through ISRs and a memory scrubber, including added logic for excessive external EDAC interrupts. This directly supports the higher-level requirement because detecting and correcting or managing failures is necessary for the DPU-BOOT CSC to continue toward completing its normal execution sequence after a failure is detected.

higher_level_requirement: The Bootstrap Monitor of the DPU-BOOT CSC shall output an error message to the RS-232 interface if an incorrect number of command arguments are entered.
lower_level_requirement: Install Project-Specific Module Error IdentifiersIn order to provide a mechanism by which error numbers can be unique across device drivers and applications, each error number must contain a unique module identifier in the most significant word of the error number. label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement establishes the project-specific structure for error identifiers, ensuring that errors generated by modules can be uniquely identified. This supports the higher-level requirement by enabling the Bootstrap Monitor to report a distinct error condition, such as an incorrect number of command arguments, through its error messaging mechanism. Although it does not specify the RS-232 output behavior, it provides the necessary error identification convention used by such error messages.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall put the processor into diagnostic mode.
lower_level_requirement: CPU BITThe CPU BIT consists of a series of tests designed to test each of the functional units of the processor. These include test for the Branch-Unit, the Fixed-Point Unit, the Floating-Point Unit, the Interrupt-Unit, and the Timer Unit. Each of these tests consists of executing a few selected instructions from the this functional unit. The General Purpose Registers (GPR), the Segment Registers (SR), the Counter Register (CTR), and the Condition Register are tested for stuck-bits as part of the Branch-Unit test. This is done by writing a 1s pattern (verified by reading it back) and then writing a 0s pattern (verified by reading it back).
label: trace
rationale: The higher-level requirement requires DPU-BOOT to place the processor in a diagnostic mode. The lower-level requirement defines CPU built-in test activities that exercise processor functional units and registers, which are characteristic operations performed once the processor is in diagnostic mode. Thus, it operationalizes the diagnostic-mode objective by specifying the processor diagnostics to be run.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall put the processor into diagnostic mode.
lower_level_requirement: Standard I/O InterfaceThe write primitive does not block. The buffer passed to write is written directly to the active portion of the ping pong buffer by the driver. This primitive is valid only in TEST mode. The write call will set errno to S_dci_MODE_ERROR and return ERROR if the driver is in NORMAL mode. In TEST mode, the driver returns the number of bytes written.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes behavior that is explicitly constrained to TEST mode, distinguishing it from NORMAL mode and enforcing mode-dependent access through error handling. This supports the higher-level requirement to place the processor into diagnostic mode because it defines standard I/O driver behavior that is only valid once the system is in the diagnostic/test mode context.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-1553 CSC shall address hardware modules as defined in document 1400, Company X Specification for the Company X Communication/Memory Module.
lower_level_requirement: Memory Upload and Download HandlingData can be upload to several types of locations, including* DRAM* EEPROM* hardware registers, and* EEPROM filesystem.ial D_MEM_DAT_UPLD command specify the target location. If the destination is the EEPROM filesystem, a block number is provided in lieu of a memory address , which is used by the DPU FSW to formulate a filename of the form eefs1:DPU_blk.##, where ## is the block number. In this case, once the entirety of the uploaded data is received by the DPU FSW, the uploaded data is then written to that file in the EEPROM filesystem. If a file already exists with that name, it is overwritten. The EEPROM filesystem can be reinitialized using the command D_MEM_DISK_INIT.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes addressing hardware-related memory destinations by specifying how memory upload/download commands target DRAM, EEPROM, hardware registers, and EEPROM filesystem locations. By defining destination selection, address/block handling, and EEPROM filesystem behavior, it provides concrete mechanisms for accessing the hardware module memory resources referenced by the higher-level requirement.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall strobe the Watchdog timer by writing to the SCM_WDR at an interval of 1 second.
lower_level_requirement: Watchdog LibraryThis function strobes the system watchdog to prevent a watchdog reset.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly implements the watchdog-strobing behavior required by the higher-level requirement by providing a function that strobes the system watchdog to prevent reset. Although it does not restate the specific SCM_WDR register or 1-second interval, its described purpose is the operational mechanism needed to satisfy the DPU-CCM watchdog strobe requirement.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall provide the capability to echo to the spacecraft each received command from the spacecraft or the ICU.
lower_level_requirement: Command HandlingCommands are dequeued from the Command Queue and executed by the Command Dispatch Task, ccmCmdTask(). This task blocks on a semaphore which is given by ccmCmdEnq(). The ccmCmdTask() wakes on the semaphore and calls ccmCmdProcess() to process waiting commands. The ccmCmdProcess() function subsequently retrieves waiting commands from the Command Queue and invokes ccmCmdDispatch() to verify the expected length of the command and execute it. If command echo is enabled, ccmCmdDispatch() will call ccmHkMkCmdEcho() to blindly echo the command back to the ground. Counts for both rejected and executed commands are maintained. If the command sent to ccmCmdEnq() is either a 1 Hz Clock Time message or an Attitude message from the spacecraft, the command will not be forwarded to the Command Queue, but instead will be executed directly while still in interrupt context. Attitude messages are forwarded to dpaCommandSend(), while the 1 Hz Clock Time messages parameters are passed to tisTimeSync() in order to synchronize the current time. Any other non DPU or spacecraft observatory messages are quietly discarded without reporting an error.In order to guarantee that ccmCmdTask() task reports in with the CCM Control Task periodically in absence of a ground command, the semaphore has a timeout value of 20 seconds. If the semaphore times out, the task will verify no commands are on the Command Queue, and then report in to the CCM Control Task by calling ccmTaskReport().
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes the echo capability by specifying that, when command echo is enabled, ccmCmdDispatch() calls ccmHkMkCmdEcho() to echo the command back. It also describes the command handling path from queue retrieval through dispatch, identifying where received commands are processed before being echoed. This provides the concrete implementation mechanism supporting the higher-level requirement to echo received commands.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall provide the capability to echo to the spacecraft each received command from the spacecraft or the ICU.
lower_level_requirement: Time SynchronizationThe interface with the spacecraft as described in document 1143-EI-S19121 specifies that the spacecraft will provide a Clock Message to each Instrument at a 1 Hz rate. The Clock Message contains both two values: a value representing the current spacecraft time, and a value representing the delta from the spacecraft time and the Univeral Time (UT), based on an epoch of TBD.
label: trace
rationale: The higher-level requirement concerns interaction between the DPU-CCM and the spacecraft, specifically handling communications received from the spacecraft. The lower-level requirement refines this spacecraft interface by specifying a recurring spacecraft-provided Clock Message and its contents, which is a concrete type of received spacecraft command/message that the DPU-CCM would need to handle within that interface. Thus it directly supports the communication capability required at the higher level.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall quietly discard any unrecognized observatory messages (I.e. messages which do not have a DPU command APID).
lower_level_requirement: Data ProcessingWhen the DCX CSC compresses a data package, the given APID is incremented by one. If the compressed copy of data is larger than original data set, the original data set will be forwarded to the SCUI CSC, an event S_dcx_UNC_USED is enqueued to ccmErrEnq(), and the APID is not incremented. In this way, the ground systems can discern compressed packets from non-compressed packets.
label: trace
rationale: The higher-level requirement concerns how the DPU-CCM distinguishes messages with a valid DPU command APID from unrecognized observatory messages that must be discarded. The lower-level requirement specifies APID handling for data packets, including when an APID is incremented for compressed data and when it remains unchanged for uncompressed forwarding. This directly supports the higher-level APID-based message recognition behavior by defining how APIDs are assigned or preserved so downstream systems can classify packet types correctly.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall collect DPU_HK and forward it to the DPU-SCUI.
lower_level_requirement: Error Collection and ReportingThe DPU-CCM CSC provides a centralized error reporting interface, ccmErrEnq(), that other FSW tasks use to report errors. Each time it wakes, ccmTask() checks to see if it is time to form an error/event packet for transmission to the ground. If so, ccmTask() calls ccmHkMkError() to actually create the packet and forward it to DPU-SCUI for transmission to the ground.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly contributes to the higher-level requirement by specifying a DPU-CCM housekeeping-related function that creates an error/event packet and forwards it to DPU-SCUI. The call to ccmHkMkError() operationalizes the collection/forming of DPU_HK content for a specific error/event housekeeping case, and the forwarding destination matches DPU-SCUI.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall process real-time non-deferred commands within B ms of receipt from the ICU or the SCU.
lower_level_requirement: Command and Control CSCThe Command and Control (CCM) CSC is a Level 2 reuse component from the INSTRUMENT Y project. The Command and Control CSC includes the following components:* A Control Task, ccmCtrlTask(), which initializes the DPU FSW and spawns other tasks at bootup, schedules the production of DPU housekeeping data packets, monitors the execution of other tasks, and schedules the execution of other periodic tasks such as the heartbeat message and the watchdog strobe; and* A Command Dispatch Task, ccmCmdTask(), which receives and dispatches real-time commands received from the SCU or the ICU.Major data structures include:* A Static Data table that keeps track of the operational state. Data included in this table includes housekeeping production rates, CCM specific flags, and the number of commands executed.* A Command Queue into which commands are placed when they arrive, via interrupt, from the ICU or the SCU.* An Error/Event Queue which accumulates error and event codes which are reported by the DPU FSW. These error and event codes are removed from the queue and placed into a telemetry packet at a given interval and included in DPU housekeeping data.DPUSDS5.12.1.1.1Flight Software InitializationThe Command and Control CSC is initialized by spawning the CCM Control Task, ccmCtrlTask(), from the operating system startup task, usrRoot(). After the task is spawned it calls a function, ccmInit(), which creates the error/event queue, instantiates needed semaphores and installs various ISRs. Finally, it spawns the remaining tasks which comprise the DPU FSW. When the CCM Control Task starts up, it reads DPU configuration startup defaults from the SYSTEM_CONFIG_AREA in EEPROM. If the SYSTEM_CONFIG_AREA checksum is bad, hard-coded defaults are used. The CCM Control Task initializes the remaining CSCs by calling the applicable initialization function, or if the CSC has an associated task, by spawning the task using the VxWorks function, taskSpawn(). When the CCM Control Task initializes a CSC, it passes the startup defaults read from EEPROM as parameters to the task initialization function. In addition to its task initialization activities, ccmInit(), also initializes the command length verification table by calling ccmCmdLengthInit(). The command processor uses the created table to verify expected command lengths for newly received commands.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly supports the higher-level timing requirement by defining the Command Dispatch Task, ccmCmdTask(), as the component that receives and dispatches real-time commands from the SCU or ICU. It also describes the command queue used when such commands arrive and the initialization of command-processing infrastructure, which operationalizes the mechanism needed to process non-deferred commands after receipt. Although it does not state the B ms bound itself, it specifies the relevant CCM functionality responsible for handling those real-time commands.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall, in rejecting a command, report an error in DPU_HK indicating the byte-code of the command being rejected in the LSB of the errno as described in 03691-DPUSDP-01.
lower_level_requirement: Error RecoveryExcept for the modification described in Sections 5.2.3.6, no further modifications to the existing task error-handling mechanisms are required. VxWorks? uses a global mechanism for returning status codes when errors occur. This is accomplished by using the task variable, errno (stored in the task control block). Most VxWorks? functions return a STATUS value. This value can either be OK or ERROR. If a function returns ERROR, then the errno variable must indicate a specific error code.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement addresses the error-handling mechanism centered on the task variable errno, specifying that when an error occurs, errno must contain a specific error code. This directly supports the higher-level requirement’s need to report command rejection information through errno in DPU_HK, since the rejected command byte-code is to be encoded in the least significant byte of that error value. The lower-level text therefore provides the operational error-status mechanism needed to implement the higher-level reporting behavior.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-CCM shall use DPU-EEPRM to access the EEPROM.
lower_level_requirement: Real-Time Clock InterfaceThe Real-Time Clock (RTC) Registers of the RAD6000 are special-purpose registers not normally accessible to C language programs. Some assembler wrapper functions provide access to these.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement specifies low-level access mechanisms to hardware-resident registers that are not directly accessible from C code, using assembler wrapper functions. This supports the higher-level requirement because accessing EEPROM through DPU-EEPRM similarly requires an implementation-level interface between DPU-CCM software and protected or special-purpose hardware-access functionality. Thus, the lower-level requirement refines the kind of wrapper/interface support needed for DPU-CCM to use DPU-EEPRM for EEPROM access.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TMALI shall allocate a ring buffer of size specified by TMALI_BUFFER_SIZE provided during initialization for storing incoming frames of data. The default buffer size shall be 15 MB.
lower_level_requirement: Public FunctionsThis task initializes the TMALI CSC and then continues to read data from the DCI and store it in the TMALI buffer each time the DCI driver signals that data is available in the Ping-Pong buffer. The availability of data in the DCI Ping-Pong buffer is signaled to the tmaliTask using a semaphore. Unless a fatal error is detected during initialization this task will never terminate.The specified 3 parameters specify the size of the TMALI queue and the initial parameters for the DCI, if the specified values are outside the allowed range default values will be used.The specified QueueSize is the allocated buffersize (in 4 byte EVENTS), the ring buffer is full when QueueSize-1 EVENTS are stored in the buffer.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes the higher-level buffer allocation behavior by specifying that the task initializes TMALI, allocates the TMALI queue/buffer according to the QueueSize parameter, and uses default values when provided values are outside the allowed range. It also states that incoming DCI data is stored in the TMALI buffer and characterizes the buffer as a ring buffer by defining its full condition as QueueSize-1 events. Thus it refines both the configurable buffer size aspect and the use of that buffer for incoming frame/data storage.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TMALI shall configure the DCI interface data timeout at startup as specified by TMALI_TIMEOUT provided during initialization. The default value shall be N milliseconds and shall be capable of being modified dynamically.
lower_level_requirement: Public FunctionsThis routine provides a means to set the bit arrangement used by the DCI. When bSpecialArrangement is TRUE, the DCI is set to special bit arrangement mode, otherwise the default mode of no rearrangement is set.

rationale: The lower-level requirement defines a public configuration routine for the DCI interface, allowing DCI behavior to be set programmatically rather than fixed. This supports the higher-level requirement’s expectation that DCI interface parameters are configured during initialization and can be modified, by specifying an operational mechanism for changing a DCI configuration mode. Although it addresses bit arrangement rather than the timeout value itself, it directly contributes to the same DCI interface configurability scope.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TMALI shall install a callback routine to respond to the DCI Error Interrupt.
lower_level_requirement: Install Exception HandlersThis routine installs a hook routine for the Memory Error Interrupt. The hook routine will be called from the interrupt context. This function returns OK always.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement specifies installing a hook/exception handler routine for an interrupt condition, and states that the routine is invoked from interrupt context. This operationalizes the higher-level requirement to install a callback routine to respond to an error interrupt, despite the lower-level text naming the Memory Error Interrupt rather than the DCI Error Interrupt. The direct semantic link is the installation of an interrupt-response callback/handler for an error interrupt.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-SCUI shall compute a CHKS16 for telecommands received from the SCU. If the CHKS16 does not match the value included in the telecommand, an error will be reported to DPU-CCM. If the checksum computes correctly, the command will be forwarded to DPU-CCM for execution.
lower_level_requirement: SCU Interface CSCThis CSC performs rate-buffering of the downlink telemetry to the SCU according to a commandable parameter. The rate at which the SCU polls the DPU is also commandable. The CSC installs an ISR to collect telecommands from the SCU via the MIL STD 1553B Interface.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly supports the higher-level telecommand-processing behavior by defining the SCU Interface CSC as the component that collects telecommands from the SCU via the MIL-STD-1553B interface. This collection mechanism is a necessary operational step before the DPU-SCUI can compute CHKS16, report checksum errors, or forward valid commands to DPU-CCM. Although it does not describe the checksum logic itself, it establishes the specific interface function that supplies the received telecommands governed by the higher-level requirement.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-TIS shall provide the capability for an application program to set the value of the SC_TIME register(s) on the SCM and enable the 1PPS clock jam register, if automatic time synchronization is enabled.
lower_level_requirement: Time Interface ConfigurationThe TIS CSC utilizes the manual jam bit in the DCI CSR to indicate whether automatic time synchronization is enabled or disabled. If automatic time synchronization is enabled, and a command is issued to manually jam the DPU clock, the command will be rejected - see tisTimeSet().
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes the higher-level condition around automatic time synchronization by specifying how the TIS determines whether that mode is enabled, using the manual jam bit in the DCI CSR. It also defines the behavior of the time-setting command under that condition, linking directly to the higher-level capability involving setting time-related registers and clock jam control when automatic synchronization is enabled.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-ICUI shall check the length of a received DPU_CMD against the message length determined by the Inter-Block Gap. If the received value does not match, then the command will be discarded, and an error will be enqueued to DPU-CCM, and a NAK message transmitted to the ICU within a second.
lower_level_requirement: Receiving Commands from the ICUThe interface to the ICU is via a synchronous serial interface (SSI) bus, which utilizes an inter-block gap (IBG) to delineate complete messages from one another. The DPU hardware produces an interrupt when it detects an IBG, and the SSI Driver provides a mechanism by which an application can install an interrupt hook routine to respond to an IBG interrupt. Upon initialization, the ICUI CSC installs a hook routine into the SSI Driver called icuiCommandReceiveISR(), which verifies the checksum of an incoming command, transmits an ACK/NAK message to the ICU, and then enqueues the command for later processing by calling ccmCmdEnq().
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes reception of ICU commands over the SSI interface using the Inter-Block Gap as the delimiter for complete messages, which is the condition used by the higher-level requirement to determine message length. It also specifies the ICUI interrupt routine behavior of transmitting ACK/NAK responses and enqueuing command-related information through ccmCmdEnq(), directly supporting the higher-level requirement’s error/NAK handling path when received command validation fails.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-ICUI shall use DPU-SSI to communicate with the SSI Interface.
lower_level_requirement: Receiving Commands from the ICUThe interface to the ICU is via a synchronous serial interface (SSI) bus, which utilizes an inter-block gap (IBG) to delineate complete messages from one another. The DPU hardware produces an interrupt when it detects an IBG, and the SSI Driver provides a mechanism by which an application can install an interrupt hook routine to respond to an IBG interrupt. Upon initialization, the ICUI CSC installs a hook routine into the SSI Driver called icuiCommandReceiveISR(), which verifies the checksum of an incoming command, transmits an ACK/NAK message to the ICU, and then enqueues the command for later processing by calling ccmCmdEnq().
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes communication between the DPU-ICUI and the SSI Interface by specifying that the ICU interface uses an SSI bus and that the ICUI CSC installs a hook routine into the SSI Driver. It describes how incoming SSI messages are detected via IBG interrupts and handled by ICUI through the SSI Driver, including checksum verification, ACK/NAK transmission, and command enqueueing. These behaviors concretely implement the higher-level requirement that DPU-ICUI use DPU-SSI to communicate with the SSI Interface.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-ICUI shall install an ISR to be invoked on the SSI receiver interblock gap interrupt, for the receiving and processing of commands from the ICU.
lower_level_requirement: Public FunctionsThis routine is called by the MIL-STD-1553 Command ISR and the SSI Interface ISR any time a command arrives from the SCU or the ICU, to enqueue the command and to wakeup the CCM Command Dispatch Task so that the command can be executed.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly supports the higher-level requirement’s objective of handling commands received from the ICU via the SSI-related interrupt path. While the higher-level requirement specifies installing an ISR invoked on the SSI receiver interblock gap interrupt, the lower-level requirement describes the routine called by the SSI Interface ISR when an ICU command arrives to enqueue it and wake the command dispatch task for execution. Thus, it refines the processing behavior performed after the ISR is invoked for received ICU commands.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-ICUI shall install an ISR to be invoked on the SSI receiver interblock gap interrupt, for the receiving and processing of commands from the ICU.
lower_level_requirement: Public FunctionsThis routine initializes the interface to the ICU. This routine opens SSI Driver port, installs the SSI interface interrupt callbacks, and enables Transmit Message Mode in the SSI Driver.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes the higher-level requirement by specifying initialization of the ICU interface, including opening the SSI driver port and installing SSI interface interrupt callbacks. Installing these callbacks is the implementation-level mechanism corresponding to installing an ISR for SSI-related interrupts, enabling command reception and processing from the ICU. Enabling transmit message mode and setting up the SSI port further supports the communication interface required by the higher-level behavior.

higher_level_requirement: The raw event list engineering mode shall collect events for transmission to the ground.
lower_level_requirement: Data ProcessingData requiring compression is received via the dcxEnq() function, which has an API definition which matches the scuiEnq() API. The DCX CSC handles the PKG_CTRL flags as described below:* PKG_COMPRESS this flag is set to indicate if the package is actually compressed.* PKG_PRIORITY_HIGH this flag is ignored by the DCX CSC but is forwarded to the SCUI CSC.* PKG_SEGMENT this flag is ignored by the DCX CSC but is forwarded to the SCUI CSC.PKG_CHECKSUM if set, the dcxEnq() function will compute a checksum which is appended to the data, and then the flag is negated. The checksum will be compressed with the rest of the data, so that when the data is decompressed on the ground, the checksum can be recomputed and compared to provide a good indication of whether the decompressed copy of the data matches the original data set.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement defines how data packages are accepted for compression and prepared for delivery through the interface that forwards relevant package controls onward. Its checksum behavior specifically supports reliable ground reconstruction after decompression, which directly contributes to collecting event data in a form suitable for transmission to and use on the ground. Thus it operationalizes part of the raw event list engineering mode’s transmission preparation responsibilities.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-DPA shall be capable of collecting detector events over the full FOV.
lower_level_requirement: Intensifier Characteristics (IC) Engineering ModeThe purpose of Intensifier Characteristics Engineering Mode is to assess detector health and performance. Detector events produced in Full Frame High Resolution detector format are collected and histogrammed for a commanded integration time to produce a pulse-height histogram.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly supports the higher-level capability by specifying a mode in which detector events are collected in Full Frame High Resolution detector format, which corresponds to collection across the detector field. It operationalizes event collection by defining that the events are accumulated over a commanded integration time and histogrammed into a pulse-height histogram. This provides a concrete implementation context for collecting detector events over the full FOV.

higher_level_requirement: There DPU-DPA shall have three science modes, X, Y mode, and X/Y mode.
lower_level_requirement: Instrument Y ProcessingThe Instrument Y Processor Task will perform tracking by breaking the exposure up into 10-second sub-exposures which are shifted and added into a final histogrammed Instrument Y. Tracking is performed by choosing guide stars from the first 10-second Instrument Y of an exposure. Then in each subsequent Instrument Y, these guide stars are found and the drift is determined by comparing the two Instrument Ys. The Instrument Y is then shifted by the determined drift and added to the previous Instrument Ys in the accumulation buffer.
label: trace
rationale: The higher-level requirement establishes that the DPU-DPA must support a distinct Y science mode. The lower-level requirement defines the processing behavior specific to Instrument Y exposures, including tracking, drift correction, and accumulation into a final histogrammed Instrument Y product. This operationalizes part of the Y mode functionality and therefore directly contributes to implementing one of the required science modes.

higher_level_requirement: The image mode shall shift successive frames according to the calculated spacecraft drift and co-add the frame into an accumulated image.
lower_level_requirement: Data Transfer to QueueDuring initialization, the TMALI CSC installs an ISR hook routine, tmaliTransferToQueueISR(), into the DCI Driver which is invoked when:* the DCI interface reaches the programmed frame limit in the Ping-Pong buffer, or* the DCI interface detects a data receipt timeout.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement defines the interrupt-driven transfer mechanism that makes received image frame data available from the DCI Ping-Pong buffer when a frame limit or timeout occurs. This directly supports the higher-level image-mode behavior because successive frames must first be captured and queued before they can be shifted according to spacecraft drift and co-added into the accumulated image.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-RTOS shall provide a function to allow an application program to read from the Real-Time Clock registers on the RAD6000SC CPU Module.
lower_level_requirement: Real-Time Clock InterfaceThe Real-Time Clock (RTC) Registers of the RAD6000 are special-purpose registers not normally accessible to C language programs. Some assembler wrapper functions provide access to these.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly supports the higher-level requirement by specifying the mechanism used to access the RAD6000 Real-Time Clock registers, which are otherwise not accessible from C programs. The assembler wrapper functions operationalize the required DPU-RTOS function that allows an application program to read those RTC registers.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BIT shall test the Error Detection and Correction (EDAC) on the Company X Communication/Memory Module by reading preprogrammed error locations in PROM.
lower_level_requirement: DRAM BITPart of the memory is tested in Boot Sequence 1, and part of the memory is tested during Boot Sequence 2. During Boot Sequence 1, ? KB of DRAM is tested before the Bootstrap is copied to this area. During Boot Sequence 2, the remaining memory is tested in ? KB blocks. The DRAM BIT first writes the address of each word in a block to that word in the block. Then the test flushes the cache and reads back the entire block. If a single-bit error occurs on the read-back, the location is read again. If another single-bit error occurs, the test assumes a hard error and marks the whole block bad. If a multiple-bit error occurs, the whole block is marked bad. If the value read back does not match the address, the whole block is marked bad. This same process is repeated with the ones complement of the address. The Bootstrap stores the results of the DRAM BIT in EEPROM as a series of x consecutive y-bit words. Each bit in a result word represents the result of testing a ? KB block of DRAM. These bits are mapped to DRAM by proceeding from least-significant bit (LSb) to most-significant bit (MSb) as the addresses of the memory blocks increase. A set bit indicates that a block of DRAM has failed. A clear bit indicates that a block of DRAM has passed the test.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes memory BIT behavior that detects and classifies single-bit and multiple-bit memory errors during read-back, which directly supports testing EDAC-related error handling. It also specifies how failed memory blocks are identified and recorded, providing concrete mechanisms for the higher-level requirement’s objective of testing error detection/correction behavior on the communication/memory module. Although it concerns DRAM rather than PROM locations specifically, its explicit handling of single-bit and multiple-bit error detection makes it a traceable refinement of the EDAC test capability.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-ADC shall create a fixed analog conversion scan list containing the A DPU analog values (active values plus one ground reference value).
lower_level_requirement: Performing Analog-to-Digital ConversionsThe ADC Driver maintains an array of ADC_LIST_ENTRY data structures which contain the hardware multiplexer setup information for each of the x analog inputs, and the current value (ADC_VALUE) of each analog input. To update a single value in the list, an application must call the update function adcUpdateNext(). The ADC hardware only has a single A/D channel, and so to perform an A/D conversion the hardware requires a multiplexer setup and corresponding settle time, as well as the normal A/D conversion time. Therefore, it takes two calls to adcUpdateNext() to update a single value in the list. To keep the driver simple and to avoid embedding hard waits in the driver, the application is required to implement the setup and conversion time by spacing successive calls to the adcUpdateNext() function appropriately.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement directly operationalizes the fixed analog conversion scan list by specifying that the ADC Driver maintains an array of ADC_LIST_ENTRY structures for each analog input, including multiplexer setup information and current ADC values. It further defines how entries in that list are updated through adcUpdateNext(), including the sequencing constraints imposed by the single A/D channel and required settle/conversion timing. This provides the concrete implementation mechanism for scanning and maintaining the DPU analog values described by the higher-level requirement.

Thus, it directly supports the DPU-DCI requirement that writes to DCI Memory occur only as B-bit words.

higher_level_requirement: Add/Remove Task links; Tasks can be linked with one another to indicate the sequence in which they have to be performed.
